query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing the nozzle-to-substrate distance on the HVAF-i7 system (to around 300–350 mm) will boost particle velocity and deposition efficiency, thereby overcoming the thickness limitation for FeCoNiCrAl bond coats while retaining coating integrity and minimal oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock produced with a 15–45 μm particle size range, as used previously with the HVAF-M3 torch.
generation.intervention: Adjust the HVAF-i7 spray parameters by increasing the nozzle-to-substrate distance to approximately 300–350 mm (from the default setting) to enhance particle velocity during deposition.
generation.conditions: The modified HVAF-i7 deposition is carried out under the same processing atmosphere and feedstock conditions as the baseline, and the coating is applied onto substrates (including internal diameters as small as 120 mm) intended for elevated-temperature thermal-barrier service with minimal in-spray oxidation.
generation.structural_mediator: Higher particle velocity increases the impact energy of molten particles, resulting in improved flattening, bonding, and packing efficiency that contributes to a thicker, adherent coating.
generation.mechanism: By increasing the nozzle distance, particles have a longer flight path, thereby accelerating to higher velocities. This enhanced kinetic energy upon impact leads to increased deposition efficiency and thicker build-up, while the reduced residence time in the oxygen-rich spray environment helps limit excessive oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to coatings deposited with the default HVAF-i7 settings (and the 15–45 μm baseline used with HVAF-M3), the intervention is predicted to yield a thicker bond coat with maintained coating integrity and low as-sprayed oxidation.
generation.baseline: FeCoNiCrAl coatings deposited using the HVAF-M3 torch with a 15–45 μm feedstock, which achieved acceptable quality and thickness, versus the inadequate thickness observed when using the same feedstock with the HVAF-i7 under default settings.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective provided that the oxygen content and other process conditions remain controlled, and the material is sprayed onto substrates (including those with internal diameters as small as 120 mm) under elevated-temperature service conditions.
generation.uncertainty: While evidence from conventional MCrAlY studies suggests a modest gain in deposition efficiency at these nozzle distances, the exact optimal distance for the HVAF-i7 system and the quantitative improvement in coating thickness remain to be determined.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of FeCoNiCrAl coatings using the HVAF-i7 torch: one set using the default nozzle-to-substrate distance and the other set using an increased distance of 300–350 mm. All other processing parameters (feedstock, gas composition, substrate pre-treatment, etc.) are held constant. Coat substrates that include internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
measurements: Measure the coating thickness using cross-sectional microscopy.
Assess deposition efficiency (mass gain per spray cycle).
Characterize the microstructure (porosity, oxidation level, adhesion) via SEM and XRD.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the increased nozzle distance does not result in a statistically significant increase in coating thickness and deposition efficiency—without compromising microstructural integrity and adhesion—compared to the default HVAF-i7 settings, then the hypothesis is falsified.
